leading_reality.hypothesis: The practical release route is a root-anchored private fixed SQLite runtime whose exact mapped bytes are admitted before Frank persistence code, with the safety claim and object-identity claim composed over the same runtime context.
leading_reality.mechanism: Pin upstream-fixed SQLite bytes and provenance, bind them to a root-owned immutable deployment anchor, verify the actually mapped object rather than an ldd prediction, then emit a composite receipt that also carries the safety basis.

counter_reality.hypothesis: Separate identity and safety workflows can each be correct yet fail to prove that the safety predicate applies to the same runtime object consumed by Frank.
counter_reality.falsifier: A same-process composite receipt binds exact tested Frank SHA, mapped libsqlite dev/inode/hash, anchor hash/fields, SQLite source-id/version, and one accepted safety basis; any mismatch or absent basis exits non-success.

alternative_reality.hypothesis: Frank may safely retain SQLite 3.45.1 if machine-checked production topology proves the documented WAL-reset trigger conditions unreachable.

unusual_experiment.scope: local disposable loader-spoof falsifier; no production or canonical Frank state mutation
unusual_experiment.result: A substitute libsqlite object can report both a chosen semantic version and chosen source-id; resolved mapped/backing identity plus byte hash is therefore required in addition to version/source-id metadata.
unusual_experiment.rollback: temporary library and loader environment removed; baseline restored
